banlist.intro: Banning certain cards aims to preserve the balance and integrity of the format. When a card generates excessive advantage, reduces interaction, or limits strategic diversity, it can harm the quality of games. Bans help maintain a healthy, competitive environment true to the format's spirit.

rules.faqSubtitle: The questions that come up at tournaments.

faq.q: Can I play a partner or a Background?
faq.a: Yes. A Background counts as a commander (rule 2.4) and partner mechanics work normally. The deck then holds 98 cards plus both commanders, for 100 total. Note that only one of your commanders may be cast from the command zone per game — the first one cast (rule 2.5).

faq.q: Is a card printed at common only on Arena legal?
faq.a: No. Rarity is read from legal paper or Magic Online printings (rule 1.4). An Arena-only rarity counts for nothing: it cannot make a card common, nor make a commander uncommon.

faq.q: Does my commander have to be legendary?
faq.a: No, and that is what makes the format. Any Creature, Vehicle, Spacecraft or Background printed at uncommon at least once can be your commander (rule 2.4).

faq.q: Can a card be both common and uncommon?
faq.a: Yes (rule 1.4.c). A card printed at common in one set and at uncommon in another can therefore be played in the deck as well as be a legal commander.

faq.q: Are cards that are not Vintage-legal playable?
faq.a: No: any card that is not legal in Vintage is banned (rule 2.8). That covers Un-set cards and cards restricted to specific formats.

faq.q: How do I check that a deck is legal?
faq.a: The site validator runs the format’s nine checks — size, singleton, rarities, color identity, ban list — against a decklist in MTGO format.

faq.q: Who goes first, and do they draw?
faq.a: The starting player skips the draw step of their first turn (rule 3.3). The London mulligan is used (rule 3.2).

rulesDoc.title: Format Rules
rulesDoc.subtitle: The Pauper Duel Commander France ruleset: deck construction, rarities and game rules.

articles.text: Pauper Duel Commander France (PDC Fr) is a two-player (1vs1) Constructed Magic: The Gathering format.
Games of Pauper Duel Commander France are played using the Magic: The Gathering Comprehensive Rules, except as modified by these rules.
Unless otherwise specified, games follow the Commander rules defined in the Magic: The Gathering Comprehensive Rules.
For the purpose of these rules, card rarities are defined as follows (you can refer to Scryfall):

sub.text: A common card is a card that has been printed at common rarity in any legal paper or Magic Online printing.
An uncommon card is a card that has been printed at uncommon rarity in any legal paper or Magic Online printing.
A card may be both a common card and an uncommon card.

articles.text: A deck consists of exactly 100 cards, including its commander(s).
Except for basic lands, a deck may not contain more than one card with the same English name.
All cards in a deck must have a color identity contained within the color identity of its commander(s).
A commander must be an Uncommon Creature, Vehicle, Spacecraft or Background (when applicable).
Players may only cast one of their commanders from the command zone per game (the first one cast).
Every non-commander card in a deck must be a common card.
Cards appearing on the Pauper Duel Commander France banned list are not legal.
Any non-legal cards in Vintage are banned.
Each player begins the game with 20 life.
The starting player skips the draw step of their first turn.
A commander may be cast from the command zone. Commander tax applies as defined by the Commander rules.

value.pitch: 100 cards, an uncommon commander, 20 life: the depth of Commander, the accessibility of Pauper.
value.eyebrow: Community format · Magic: The Gathering · 1 versus 1
value.duelText: 1v1, 20 life, no politics and no commander damage: every decision counts.
value.accessText: 99 commons and a single uncommon commander. The Pauper card pool, without the rarities that drive other formats’ prices.
value.commandersText: Any uncommon creature can be your commander — it does not need to be legendary. That is the real difference from Duel Commander.
value.singletonText: One copy per card. Deckbuilding brings back commons forgotten for twenty years.
value.livingText: A committee, a ban list with published reasoning, an announcement every two months, and tournaments across France.
